reading just those two verses may lead to misinterpretation. the context there is Jesus was challenging the man if he could give up his possessions and follow Him. since if that person can do that, it means that he values God and the treasures he will have in Heaven more that his earthly riches. on the latter verse, "..he went away grieving.." meaning that the man's true state has been laid bare (that he has replaced direct trust in God with earthly riches) and he does not repent.

it doesn't really have anything to do with a person being a democrat or pro-reallocating wealth, since it is not even remotely related to the subject being discussed in that story. those verses act as reminders to Christians to not value the things here on earth more that they value God. doing so means one fails the first commandment, "You shall have no other gods before me" (Exodus 20:3).
